meta.title: Book of Memory of the Lemko Region

howToRead.title: How to read the lists
howToRead.intro: The lists on this site follow the “Book of Memory of the Lemko Region 1944–1946”: every record is shown as printed in the book, in Ukrainian. Below, the marks and features of the records are explained, following the author's preface to the book.

chs.text: In the relationship column it means член сім’ї, “family member”. The book uses it for people recorded on their own, without a family number.

question.term: A question mark, or another reading in brackets
question.text: The archival record was hard to read, for example the year of birth 1932(30) or the name Теодор (Федір). The site's search finds a record by each of the readings.

surnames.term: Spelling of surnames and given names
surnames.text: Surnames are given as the clerks of the archival lists wrote them, so one surname may appear in several spellings. Some given names are printed in their modern form, for example Маря — Марія, Осиф — Йосиф.

years.text: Years of birth in the archival documents may be wrong. The book gives them as recorded.

areas.text: Regions are named as they were then: Ворошиловградська is now Луганська, Сталінська is now Донецька, Станіславська is now Івано-Франківська. Дрогобицька oblast was later abolished: part of it went to Львівська oblast, part to Poland.

numbering.text: The numbering of families and persons in the book differs from the archive's: families that did not leave, or were recorded twice, are left out of the book.

missing.text: Some family members were never registered in the archival lists, so a family in the book may be incomplete.

notes.text: Where a page of the archival document is damaged, the book prints a note instead of names, for example «Родина №7 - заклеєно стор. - 4 особи.» (“Family no. 7 — page pasted over — 4 persons”). The site shows such notes in italics among the family members.

howToRead.source: Source: Yaroslava Halyk, “Book of Memory of the Lemko Region 1944–1946”, vol. 3, preface.

sidebar.title: BOOK OF MEMORY OF THE LEMKO REGION 1944–1946
sidebar.text: The “Book of Memory of the Lemko Region 1944–1946” contains the lists of Ukrainian Lemkos forcibly evicted in 1944–1946 by the communist regimes of Poland and the USSR. Based on archival documents, the book preserves the memory of the Lemko tragedy and serves as a reference for the descendants of the deportees. Author: Yaroslava Halyk.

about.title: About the project
about.text1: The “Book of Memory of the Lemko Region 1944–1946” is a martyrology of the Ukrainian Lemkos who fell victim to the criminal resettlement campaign carried out by the communist regimes of Poland and the USSR in 1944–1946. As a result, hundreds of thousands of Lemkos were forcibly evicted from their ancestral ethnic lands, then under Polish rule, to the Ukrainian SSR. The lists of deported families and persons are arranged by the settlements of the Lemko Region and based on archival documents.
about.text2: This book is documentary evidence of the Lemko tragedy of the mid-20th century and a warning against similar crimes. It is an important reference for deported Lemkos and their descendants, helping them find their families. It will also be a useful resource for local historians, researchers, scholars and historians.
about.text3: Idea, project lead and compiler: Yaroslava Halyk. Photocopies of archival documents: Yaroslava Halyk, Oleh Radziievskyi (in vol. 1 also Ivan Chelak). Technical editing: Andrii Khomyn. Technical support: Denys Halyk. Typesetting: Yaroslava Halyk, Andrii Khomyn (in vol. 1 also Valeriia Halyk, Oleksii Halyk, Andrii Shafran, Fr. Taras Hrem). The book was published with the financial support of the Lemko Research Foundation in the USA.
